name: Großglockner Hochalpenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road is Austria's most iconic scenic highway, winding 48 km up to 2,571 m through the core of the Hohe Tauern National Park.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The internationally renowned Grossglockner High Alpine Road (Großglockner Hochalpenstraße) ranks among Europe's most celebrated engineering and scenic landmarks, seamlessly linking Salzburg and Carinthia with direct connections into East Tirol. Spanning 48 kilometres across 36 hairpin bends, this heritage-protected mountain pass road built during the 1930s crests the main alpine divide at elevations up to 2,571 metres. Bisecting Central Europe's largest national reserve—the Hohe Tauern National Park—the route journeys through every alpine ecological zone, from verdant dairy pastures and fragrant larch woods to arctic tundra and perennial glaciers. The undisputed centerpiece is the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe at 2,369 metres: from its vast tiered terraces, visitors gaze directly upon the 3,798-metre glaciated peak of the Grossglockner—Austria's highest mountain—and the creeping Pasterze glacier. Engaging museums, wildlife trails, and panoramic restaurants render the journey an indelible highlight.

Route & Anforderungen

Driving the highway is comfortable and rewarding in any roadworthy passenger car, motorbike, or campervan. The road is broad, flawlessly paved, lined with safety barriers, and features manageable maximum gradients around twelve percent. With dozens of curated theme viewpoints, alpine exhibits, and inns flanking the road, drivers should budget four to six hours for a leisurely crossing. Barrier-free pathways encircle the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe visitor hub; those wishing to hike along the trail towards the Pasterze glacier tongue require ankle-high hiking boots with rubber traction. High altitude winds frequently chill the summit ridges (Hochtor tunnel at 2,504 m and Edelweißspitze at 2,571 m), making warm layers indispensable.

Besuch & Anreise

Access is gained from the south via Heiligenblut (conveniently reached from East Tirol via Lienz across the Iselsberg Pass) or from the north via Fusch an der Glocknerstraße near Zell am See. Toll plazas are located at Ferleiten and Heiligenblut. Spacious multi-storey parking garages at Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe are complimentary for toll-ticket holders.

Tipps

Keep a keen eye open around the sunlit slopes of the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe for charming wild alpine marmots basking on the rocks. Motorists comfortable with tight turns should navigate the historic spur road up to the cobbled Edelweißspitze, rewarding them with views over thirty distinct 3,000-metre peaks.
preis: Toll road applies vehicle charges (day passes for passenger cars, motorbikes, and EVs)
oeffnungszeiten: Open seasonally early May through early November (weather dependent)
